ds_methods_kb.when_to_apply: When numerical column has missing null values and skewness is low (between -1.0 and +1.0).
ds_methods_kb.why_to_apply: Preserves dataset sample size without altering mean distribution for normally distributed data.
ds_methods_kb.how_to_apply: df['col'] = pd.to_numeric(df['col'], errors='coerce').fillna(df['col'].mean().round(2))

ds_methods_kb.when_to_apply: When numerical column has missing null values and heavy skewness (> 1.0 or < -1.0) or extreme outliers.
ds_methods_kb.why_to_apply: Median is robust against extreme outliers and skewed distributions, unlike Mean.
ds_methods_kb.how_to_apply: df['col'] = pd.to_numeric(df['col'], errors='coerce').fillna(df['col'].median().round(2))

ds_methods_kb.when_to_apply: When categorical (string/object) column has missing null values.
ds_methods_kb.why_to_apply: Replaces missing categories with the most frequent value without introducing invalid levels.
ds_methods_kb.how_to_apply: df['col'] = df['col'].fillna(df['col'].mode()[0])

ds_methods_kb.when_to_apply: When continuous numeric features contain extreme high/low values beyond [Q1 - 1.5*IQR, Q3 + 1.5*IQR].
ds_methods_kb.why_to_apply: Prevents extreme outliers from corrupting Machine Learning model weights while retaining row count.
ds_methods_kb.how_to_apply:
Q1 = df['col'].quantile(0.25)
Q3 = df['col'].quantile(0.75)
IQR = Q3 - Q1
df['col'] = df['col'].clip(lower=Q1-1.5*IQR, upper=Q3+1.5*IQR)

ds_methods_kb.when_to_apply: When categorical feature has nominal (unordered) text categories and unique levels < 20.
ds_methods_kb.why_to_apply: Converts categorical strings into numerical binary dummy columns required by linear & tree models.
ds_methods_kb.how_to_apply: df = pd.get_dummies(df, columns=['col'], drop_first=True, dtype=int)

ds_methods_kb.when_to_apply: When features have varying numeric scales before training Distance/Gradient models (KNN, SVM, Linear Regression).
ds_methods_kb.why_to_apply: Transforms features to mean=0 and variance=1 so large magnitude features do not dominate model learning.
ds_methods_kb.how_to_apply:
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
scaler = StandardScaler()
X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X)

ds_methods_kb.when_to_apply: When target label is discrete categorical (Classification) or continuous numeric float (Regression).
ds_methods_kb.why_to_apply: Ensemble of decision trees that reduces variance, resists overfitting, and measures feature importances.
ds_methods_kb.how_to_apply:
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
model = RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=100, random_state=42)
model.fit(X_train, y_train)

ds_methods_kb.when_to_apply: When analyzing frequency distribution, bell-curve normality, and skewness of a numeric column.
ds_methods_kb.why_to_apply: Visually confirms whether a feature is Gaussian or skewed before deciding imputation strategy.
ds_methods_kb.how_to_apply:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
plt.hist(df['col'], bins=20, color='skyblue', edgecolor='black')
plt.title('Distribution of col')
plt.show()

ds_methods_kb.when_to_apply: When identifying extreme outlier points, median, and interquartile range boundaries.
ds_methods_kb.why_to_apply: Displays five-number summary (Min, Q1, Median, Q3, Max) and isolated outlier dots.
ds_methods_kb.how_to_apply:
import seaborn as sns
sns.boxplot(x=df['col'], color='teal')
plt.title('Boxplot of col')
plt.show()

ds_methods_kb.when_to_apply: When assessing linear/non-linear relationships between two continuous numeric features.
ds_methods_kb.why_to_apply: Discovers collinearity and strong predictor candidates for target variable.
ds_methods_kb.how_to_apply:
import seaborn as sns
sns.heatmap(df.corr(), annot=True, cmap='coolwarm')
plt.show()

ds_methods_kb.when_to_apply: When discovering natural groupings, customer segments, or un-labeled clusters in data.
ds_methods_kb.why_to_apply: Partitions observations into K distinct clusters minimizing within-cluster variance (inertia).
ds_methods_kb.how_to_apply:
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
kmeans = KMeans(n_clusters=3, random_state=42)
df['Cluster'] = kmeans.fit_predict(X_scaled)

ds_methods_kb.when_to_apply: When dataset contains high-dimensional collinear features (20+ columns) that need compression for visualization.
ds_methods_kb.why_to_apply: Projects high-dimensional space onto 2 principal orthogonal axes retaining maximum variance.
ds_methods_kb.how_to_apply:
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
pca = PCA(n_components=2)
X_pca = pca.fit_transform(X_scaled)

ds_methods_kb.when_to_apply: When multiple numerical predictor columns show strong inter-correlations (VIF > 5.0).
ds_methods_kb.why_to_apply: Detects redundant predictor variables that destabilize linear regression coefficients.
ds_methods_kb.how_to_apply:
from statsmodels.stats.outliers_influence import variance_inflation_factor
vif = [variance_inflation_factor(X.values, i) for i in range(X.shape[1])]

ds_methods_kb.when_to_apply: When numeric features exhibit strong non-Gaussian skewness and contain zero or negative values.
ds_methods_kb.why_to_apply: Transforms non-normal skewed feature distributions into Gaussian bell curves to satisfy linear assumptions.
ds_methods_kb.how_to_apply:
from sklearn.preprocessing import PowerTransformer
pt = PowerTransformer(method='yeo-johnson')
df['col'] = pt.fit_transform(df[['col']])

ds_methods_kb.when_to_apply: When dataset contains timestamp strings or datetime objects.
ds_methods_kb.why_to_apply: Extracts granular temporal components (Year, Month, Day, Hour, DayOfWeek, Is_Weekend) for ML algorithms.
ds_methods_kb.how_to_apply:
df['year'] = pd.to_datetime(df['date']).dt.year
df['is_weekend'] = pd.to_datetime(df['date']).dt.dayofweek >= 5

ds_methods_kb.when_to_apply: When dataset has hundreds of feature columns and only top K informative features are needed.
ds_methods_kb.why_to_apply: Ranks features using ANOVA F-score or Mutual Information to eliminate uninformative noise.
ds_methods_kb.how_to_apply:
from sklearn.feature_selection import SelectKBest, f_classif
selector = SelectKBest(score_func=f_classif, k=10)
X_new = selector.fit_transform(X, y)

ds_methods_kb.when_to_apply: When visualizing aggregated group totals or percentages with exact value labels on top of bars.
ds_methods_kb.why_to_apply: Displays clean, publication-ready bar plots with high-contrast text annotations and custom color palettes.
ds_methods_kb.how_to_apply:
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
ax = sns.barplot(data=df, x='x_col', y='y_col', palette='Blues_r')
for p in ax.patches:
    ax.annotate(f'{p.get_height():.1f}', (p.get_x() + p.get_width() / 2., p.get_height()), ha='center', va='center', xytext=(0, 5), textcoords='offset points')
plt.show()

ds_methods_kb.when_to_apply: When testing whether a continuous numeric column follows a normal Gaussian bell curve distribution.
ds_methods_kb.why_to_apply: Computes p-value to statistically confirm Gaussian normality before parametric hypothesis testing.
ds_methods_kb.how_to_apply:
from scipy.stats import shapiro
stat, p_val = shapiro(df['col'].dropna())
print(f'Shapiro Statistic: {stat:.4f}, p-value: {p_val:.4e}')

ds_methods_kb.when_to_apply: When iteratively selecting top K features by recursively pruning non-predictive variables.
ds_methods_kb.why_to_apply: Recursively fits a model and removes the weakest features to optimize generalization score.
ds_methods_kb.how_to_apply:
from sklearn.feature_selection import RFE
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
selector = RFE(RandomForestClassifier(), n_features_to_select=5)
selector.fit(X, y)

ds_methods_kb.when_to_apply: When driving coefficients of uninformative collinear features exactly to zero.
ds_methods_kb.why_to_apply: Applies L1 regularization penalty to perform automated feature pruning.
ds_methods_kb.how_to_apply:
from sklearn.linear_model import LassoCV
lasso = LassoCV().fit(X, y)
selected_features = X.columns[lasso.coef_ != 0]
